work_window_utc.meaning: Parallel implementation and source review followed by focused offline checks; not live runtime or acceptance performance.

implementation: New external Linux root observer reads exactly the collector and caller-pinned worker/broker. It holds three PIDFDs and three active time-namespace descriptors, verifies process start epochs and all four UID/GID values, and checks held/named/magic-link namespace identities.

Both actual CLOCK_BOOTTIME read calls are bracketed by collector epoch, active namespace and boot/account/thread readbacks. Differing namespace identities are retained by the producer, never normalised or relabelled.

The independent consumer has no producer import. It verifies raw SHA-256 pins, canonical JSON, exact schemas, strict integer bounds, false claim ceilings, shared active namespaces, stable process identities and boot, and ordered before/after brackets.

The existing common process observer gains an additive owned-fixture wrapper. It derives worker/broker pins from actual fixed unit observations, performs one clock observation, and rechecks the entire four-role fixture before returning the unmodified clock record.
No offset translation, time_for_children substitution, latency output, event timestamp, namespace transition, service action, profile migration or final acceptance execution is added.
review_findings_resolved: The initial observer draft sampled its first clock before acquiring collector namespace custody. Static review moved sampling after all six descriptors are held and added collector-domain readbacks after the final stamp, before the first pipeline run.
A boot ID alone does not identify a common Linux time namespace. This implementation requires exact active namespace device/inode equality instead of inferring offsets or comparing clock values.
Linux timens_offsets describes the children namespace, so offset-based evidence was excluded from both producer and strict independent consumer.

The rendered worker handles receipt-only messages before actual create dispatch and retains an inherited hard-pinned artifact contract. The roadmap records that a real ingress hook requires honest successor provisioning and may not be patched into the common profile by fabricating the predecessor artifact.

reviewed_input_closure.meaning: Explicit transitive local Python sources and new test modules; wrapper reuses the old inert fixture constructor without discovering historical tests. Reviewed against recursive local AST import closure. Runner, requirements, interpreter/platform and prerequisite fingerprint are separately bound. No dynamic repository data fixtures are used.

limitations: Producer kernel/descriptor/clock operations are mocked in unit tests; no Linux readback was performed. Wrapper tests use inert unit/kernel doubles with real local descriptor lifetimes, not live systemd or PIDFD observations.
The output is external root process/namespace readback, not authenticated ingress, broker final decision, request attribution, elapsed time, causal proof, task completion or sink verification.
Both retained observations must come from the same collector process. Point-in-time read brackets do not establish continuous process/namespace immutability or hostile-root-resistant attestation.

The wrapper performs independent fixture checks but returns the producer record unchanged. Wrapper custody and installed helper source inventory still need outer controller evidence and live identity joins.

The common73 profile and frozen predecessors are unchanged. Real worker hook installation requires honest successor provisioning because the inherited preparation path independently pins the old rendered worker.
The worker ProcSubset=pid setting prevents directly reusing this external root observer as an in-process hook. The broker final-decision hook must remain free of filesystem reads.

Final31 and100-attempt/100-pair acceptance remains blocked pending runtime event/timing/workload/negative-control/sink callback integration, remaining admission and RUN/sensor semantics, and the full independent verifier inventory.
next_dependency: Integrate actual authenticated create-ingress and effective final-decision hooks with honest successor provisioning and installed-helper inventories. Wire both clock observations from one collector process and independent replay into the shared controller, then real source-pinned execute, verifier and identity callbacks into genuine prepared-attempt consumption. Do not consume ingress on receipt-only messages, fake a predecessor artifact, translate unobserved clock offsets or run final acceptance early.
checkpoint_commit: Create one signed local commit for this reviewed checked batch, verify signature and clean working tree, and retain its hash in ignored .aragorn/phase3-batch-<short-hash>-checkpoint.json. No automatic push.
